channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Taliban Ban Commemoration of General Abdul Raziq in Kandahar, Sources Say
item.description: Sources report the Taliban have banned commemorations for former Kandahar police chief General Abdul Raziq. The intelligence directorate warned his family against holding a ceremony and publishing content on social media. Defiance could lead to arrest.

item.title: OIC Chief to Continue Dialogue on Women's Rights with Afghan Interim Government
item.description: The OIC Secretary-General stated that dialogue with Afghanistan's de facto authorities on women's and girls' rights to education and work will continue, based on Islamic values. He also pledged support for humanitarian and economic needs.

item.title: UN Secretary-General's Special Representative for Afghanistan Arrives in Kabul
item.description: Rabab Fatima has arrived in Kabul to begin her duties as the UN Secretary-General’s Special Representative for Afghanistan and head of the UN Assistance Mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA). Fatima brings over 30 years of diplomatic and policy experience to the role, having been appointed on July 15, 2026.

item.title: Mullah Baradar Urges UNAMA to Impartially Report Afghanistan's Economic and Security Progress
item.description: Mullah Abdul Ghani Baradar urged the UN Assistance Mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA) to report impartially, considering the country's realities and achievements. He stated it's unfair to focus only on negatives while ignoring economic and security progress, especially amid crises like drought and displacement.

item.title: Seven Killed in Fire at Canadian Military Base During Exercise
item.description: At least seven people died and dozens were injured in an explosion and fire at the Wainwright military base in Canada. State media reported the incident occurred during live firing exercises, possibly due to damage to a gas pipeline, causing a large blaze.

item.title: Uzbekistan and UNICEF Discuss Pharmaceutical Supplies for Afghanistan
item.description: Uzbekistan's Agency for the Development of the Medical and Pharmaceutical Industry met with UNICEF to discuss expanding cooperation on medicine supplies to Afghanistan. Discussions focused on international procurement, quality standards, and transparency. The delegation visited BioPharma City and the Pharmaceutical Technical University.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Energy Sector Prepared for Winter, Officials Address Planned Power Outages
item.description: Uzbekistan's energy sector is ready for winter, with preparations beginning the previous year. Officials identified high-risk areas for repairs, categorizing them by risk level. Daily electricity consumption is nearing 200 million kWh, with summer consumption around 150 million kWh on some days. The company reported that 35% of consumers used over 200 kWh in August.

item.title: Two Killed, Ten Injured in Bus Collision with Truck Trailer in Zhetysu Region
item.description: A minibus carrying passengers collided with the trailer of a Kamaz truck on the Almaty-Ust-Kamenogorsk highway in the Zhetysu region. Two people died at the scene, and ten passengers were hospitalized with injuries. The minibus driver has been detained, and a criminal investigation has been launched into the incident.

item.title: US Secretary of State Explains Visit to Uzbekistan and 'C5+1' Meeting Amid Global Crises
item.description: US Secretary of State Antony Blinken explained his visit to Uzbekistan and the 'C5+1' meeting, emphasizing the importance of strengthening relations with Central Asian countries. He noted that while global crises often delay strategic visits, Washington prioritizes developing partnerships. The meeting brought together leaders and foreign ministers from five Central Asian nations.

item.title: Taliban Fighters Allegedly Shoot Teenager in Kandahar Civilian Vehicle
item.description: Sources in Kandahar report that Taliban fighters, disguised in civilian clothing, opened fire on a civilian vehicle at a checkpoint. One occupant, a teenager, was hit. The Taliban reportedly cordoned off the area after the incident. The teenager's identity and condition remain unknown.

item.title: Taliban Claims Responsibility for Death of Resistance Front Commander
item.description: The Taliban announced the death of a commander from the 'Resistance Front'. No further details regarding the circumstances or location of the commander's death were provided by the Taliban. The 'Resistance Front' has not yet commented on the claim.

item.title: Taliban Reportedly Moving Military Equipment to Southern Afghanistan Provinces
item.description: Sources in Kandahar indicate the Taliban are transferring military equipment, including various weapons, from Kabul and other provinces to Kandahar and Helmand. The purpose and quantity of the transferred equipment remain undisclosed by the Taliban.

item.title: Taliban Remove Nighttime Checkpoints in Lashkar Gah, Helmand Province
item.description: Sources in Helmand report the Taliban have removed all nighttime checkpoints in Lashkar Gah over the past week. Daytime checkpoints remain active, but fighters are now confined to posts at night. This follows recent grenade attacks on the provincial governor's office and a Taliban security district office, with no reported casualties. Clashes over opium smuggling also recently occurred.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov Announces Completion of Tajikistan-Kyrgyzstan Border Demarcation
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov announced the completion of border demarcation work between Tajikistan and Kyrgyzstan. He made the statement during a meeting with residents of the Batken region. The announcement comes amid ongoing efforts to resolve border disputes between the two Central Asian nations.

item.title: Samarkand Imposes Movement Restrictions for International Events
item.description: Samarkand will restrict entry and traffic on certain streets for five days due to upcoming international events. From October 18 to October 22, movement will be periodically limited on 16 central streets. Security measures are being enhanced for the duration of the events.

item.title: Petropavlovsk Thermal Power Plant to Demolish Chimney Ahead of Schedule
item.description: Petropavlovsk Thermal Power Plant-2 plans to prematurely decommission and demolish chimney No. 2. Despite technical assessments indicating usability until 2029, the plant aims to complete demolition by 2027-2028. The project, costing over 1 billion tenge, involves replacing the lining and repairing external concrete sections.

item.title: US Secretary of State to Discuss Central Asia Agenda
item.description: The US Secretary of State is scheduled to visit Central Asia. Discussions are expected to cover key regional issues, including security, economic cooperation, and diplomatic relations. The specific agenda remains undisclosed.

item.title: Massive Drone Attack Hits St. Petersburg and Leningrad Oblast, Causing Fires
item.description: A large-scale drone attack struck St. Petersburg and the Leningrad region overnight on October 18. Media reported it as one of the largest since the start of Russia's war in Ukraine. Several facilities, including oil sites, warehouses, and data centers, caught fire. One drone hit a bridge, and residential buildings were damaged. Authorities reported one fatality and five injuries.

item.title: UN Warns Over 15 Million in Afghanistan Face Acute Food Insecurity
item.description: The United Nations reports that 15.9 million people in Afghanistan are experiencing acute food insecurity, with the situation projected to worsen this winter. Approximately 3.4 million face emergency levels, and millions more are expected to be in crisis. Malnutrition among children is a significant concern.

item.title: Uzbekistan Strengthens Penalties for Involving Minors in Drug Abuse
item.description: Uzbekistan has significantly increased penalties for involving minors in drug and psychotropic substance consumption. A new law signed by the President amends the Criminal Code, raising fines and toughening imprisonment sentences. Those found guilty of luring minors into drug use could face up to 10 years in prison.

item.title: IMF Significantly Raises Tajikistan's Economic Growth Forecast for 2026 and 2027
item.description: The International Monetary Fund has substantially increased its economic growth projections for Tajikistan. The forecast for 2026 has been raised from 6% to 7.3%, and for 2027, it has been revised upwards from 4.8% to 6.8%.

item.title: UN Urges Investment in Education and Support for Afghan Children Deported from Iran
item.description: The United Nations in Afghanistan expressed concern over the deportation of adolescents from Iran. The organization called for urgent investment in education, child protection, and livelihood opportunities for families. Many Afghan children have been working in Iran and their return increases the need for educational and social support.

item.title: Trump Takes Up to 60 Days to Review New Sanctions Against Russia
item.description: US President Donald Trump will assess the impact of new restrictions against Russia and its energy buyers on the US and global economies. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated this could take up to 60 days. Trump had previously suspended the implementation of these measures.

item.title: Zelensky Discusses Potential Venue for Meeting with Putin and Trump
item.description: Ukrainian President Zelensky stated that the US is working to organize a trilateral meeting involving himself, Russian President Putin, and US President Trump. The specific location for this potential meeting has not yet been disclosed.

item.title: Samarkand to Restrict Entry and Traffic for International Events
item.description: Samarkand will temporarily restrict entry and traffic on several central streets from October 18-22 due to international events. The restrictions are for the Central Asia and US foreign ministers' meeting and a global summit on children's well-being. Emergency services will be exempt, and transit traffic will be rerouted.

item.title: 170 Tons of Cotton Burn in Turkestan Region Factory
item.description: A fire broke out at a cotton processing plant in the Turkestan region of Kazakhstan, consuming 170 tons of cotton across 242 square meters. The Ministry of Emergency Situations reported that the fire was completely extinguished. There were no casualties, and the cause of the fire is under investigation.

item.title: Taliban Health Minister Seeks Russian Cooperation in Healthcare Sector
item.description: The Taliban's acting Health Minister, Nooruljalal Jalali, met with a Russian delegation in Kabul to discuss expanding bilateral cooperation in healthcare. Jalali specifically requested Russia's assistance in enhancing the capacity of healthcare professionals, particularly in diagnosing and treating cancer and cardiovascular diseases. The Russian delegation expressed readiness to support joint health initiatives.

item.title: Digital Family Card Introduced in Kazakhstan for Social Assistance Assessment
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Labor and Social Protection is transitioning from old categories to assessing actual family needs for social assistance. The new approach, discussed in Kyzylorda, will consider income, employment, and property. These changes, effective January 1, 2027, aim to direct state aid to those genuinely in need, excluding pension provisions.

item.title: Vessel Attacked Off UAE Coast, One Injured
item.description: A small vessel was targeted by two unknown projectiles off the coast of the United Arab Emirates, resulting in one injury. The incident occurred on Sunday morning near Khor Fakkan. The tugboat sustained damage but continued its journey south. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack.

item.title: Ukrainian drones attack St. Petersburg, targeting oil terminal, airport, and data center
item.description: Ukrainian drones attacked St. Petersburg on October 18, impacting civilian infrastructure including an oil terminal, airport, and VK data center. Air defense systems were active, and emergency services responded to fires. The governor of Leningrad Oblast reported 135 drones shot down over the region.

item.title: Fire Engulfs Warehouses and Administrative Building in Almaty
item.description: A fire broke out on the premises of an enterprise in Almaty's Almaly district, initially consuming warehouse buildings before spreading to an adjacent two-story administrative structure. The blaze, covering 280 square meters, was fully extinguished overnight. No casualties were reported.

item.title: Tajikistan Prepares to Simplify International Freight Transport Procedures
item.description: Tajikistan is preparing to simplify international freight transport. A new system will allow carriers to cross multiple countries with a single permit. This initiative aims to streamline logistics and facilitate cross-border trade for businesses operating within the region.

item.title: Zelensky: Starlink Speed Limited in Ukraine, Hindering Drone Interception
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Starlink terminal speeds in Ukraine remain limited to 161 km/h, significantly slower than in neighboring European countries. He believes this deliberate slowdown hinders the interception of Russian drones, as detection requires higher speeds. Investigations are ongoing.

item.title: Pakistan Closes Border Crossings with Iran Due to Security Concerns
item.description: Local authorities in Pakistan's Balochistan province have closed the official Gabd-Reemdan and Taftan border crossings with Iran, citing security concerns and a need to prevent smuggling. The spokesperson for the provincial government stated the closure is necessary for improving security and border management. Both countries' senior officials are in contact to resolve the issues.

item.title: Criminal Case Opened Against Illegal Hunters of Red Book Bears and Boars in Surkhandarya
item.description: A criminal case has been initiated in Surkhandarya region against individuals illegally hunting protected species. During a raid, authorities found bear and wild boar remains in a vehicle, identified as a Tian Shan brown bear and three wild boars, both listed in Uzbekistan's Red Book. The estimated material damage amounts to over 679 million Uzbek soums.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Introduce Means-Testing for Certain Social Benefits from 2027
item.description: Starting January 1, 2027, Kazakhstan will implement a needs-based assessment for specific state social benefits. The Ministry of Labor and Social Protection will utilize a Digital Family Map to evaluate household well-being based on income, employment, housing, and assets. Families will be categorized, with those in the highest two tiers potentially losing access to certain benefits.

item.title: Saudi Military Helicopter Crashes, Houthi Claim Responsibility
item.description: Saudi Arabia confirmed the crash of a military helicopter, attributing it to technical failure, after the Houthi group claimed to have shot it down. The Saudi coalition spokesperson stated the helicopter crashed on Saudi territory due to technical issues, killing both pilots. The incident occurs amid escalating conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Labor Assures State Guarantees for Pension Contributions Under Private Management
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Labor and Social Protection has confirmed that state guarantees for pension contributions remain in full effect when funds are transferred to private management. While the state ensures the safety of actual contributions, individuals are responsible for investment risks associated with their chosen management company and strategy.

item.title: US Senator Marco Rubio to Meet Central Asian Foreign Ministers on Trade, Security, and Investment
item.description: US Senator Marco Rubio is visiting Central Asia to strengthen relations, focusing on strategic cooperation in economic and security spheres. He will meet with the foreign ministers of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan. Over 200 American companies are also part of the delegation.

item.title: US Ambassador Condemns Israeli Settler Attack on American Journalist
item.description: The US Ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, has labeled the attack by Israeli settlers on an American journalist as a "terrorist act." He called for a full investigation, arrests, and prosecution of those involved. The journalist sustained serious injuries during the incident while covering olive harvesting.
